{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABh_-x8A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhLXvG0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 233, "title": "Redesign the browser player UI/UX and responsive layout using snes-rust as the reference", "body": "## Problem and goal

The current pc98-rust browser frontend has grown organically: a large introductory section, demo launch buttons, several control rows, a large screen, technical captions, media/boot settings, a virtual keyboard and a long explanatory footer compete for attention. The user wants a simpler, more screen-focused experience consistent with the same author's **snes-rust** demo.

**Redesign the browser UI/UX and responsive layout using snes-rust as the concrete visual and interaction reference, while adapting the media controls to a PC-98 computer rather than copying a console cartridge UI literally.** Retain all existing emulator functionality and safeguards. The screen, not the surrounding website or configuration, should be the main attraction.

### References (inspect these before implementation)

- [snes-rust live demo](https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/)
- [snes-rust HTML](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), [CSS](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css), [application](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js), [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust#uiux)
- [Current pc98-rust live demo](https://takahirox.github.io/pc98-rust/)
- [Current HTML](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), [CSS](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/style.css), [application](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js), [presentation stage](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/presenter.js)
- #115: existing UI/UX design principles; #120/#130: media routing, boot selection and bundled FreeDOS; #191/#195: CRT presentation and default; #163/#164: 60 fps presentation; #230/#232: recent CRT performance and stereo sound work.

Apply the three shared principles: **Keep it simple. Show, don't tell. Intuitive and predictable.** Use layout, spacing and clear control grouping rather than prominent explanatory prose. Simplicity must not remove meaningful consent, accessible names, recovery actions or warnings.

## Target desktop layout

The following is the requested structure (illustrative wireframe, not a mandatory exact pixel specification):

```
pc98-rust                                             Help   GitHub

+-----------------------------------------+     Machine
|                                         |     [ PC-9821Ap      v ]
|                                         |
|            PC-98 screen                 |     IDE HDD
|            CRT by default               |     FreeDOS.hdi
|            4:3 as applicable            |     [ Change / actions ]
|                                         |
|                                         |     Floppy 1
|                                         |     Empty   [ Insert… ]
|                                         |
|                                         |     Floppy 2
+-----------------------------------------+     Empty   [ Insert… ]

[Pause] [Reset] [Mute icon] [Volume slider] [Display v] [Fullscreen]
[Keyboard] [Settings]                                     Running
```

- **Visual style:** use the restrained, light neutral background, white controls, dark text, subtle borders/radii, muted green accents and compact typography/spacing of snes-rust. Keep the emulator screen's dark surround. Avoid decorative marketing headers, oversized badges, excessive card nesting, redundant captions or simulated physical computer bezels. Adopt the same design language, not an exact replica of the SNES controller.
- **Header:** compact `pc98-rust` heading and Help/GitHub links. Remove the introductory hero ("A little machine. A new adventure.") from the primary view. Move long prose, compatibility/technical notes, licensing and keyboard instructions to Help, README or a concise secondary link as appropriate; do not lose required notices.
- **Primary screen:** on the left, visually dominant, sized to available width AND reasonable viewport height; preserve CRT/pixel aspect behavior. A desktop two-column layout should resemble snes-rust with the PC-98 media panel on the right. No avoidable scroll just to reach frequent controls at representative desktop sizes such as 1280×720 and 1440×900. Do not force the screen into a tiny area merely to fit an unusually short viewport.
- **Right-side machine/media panel:** show the machine selector and three independently identifiable slots: IDE HDD, Floppy 1, Floppy 2. Each shows the actual mounted name or Empty, relevant availability/busy state, and an obvious insert/change action. Expose per-slot Eject and Export through compact secondary actions or a contextual popover, rather than always displaying every action. Long file names truncate without changing screen geometry, with an accessible full name. Use explicit slot-specific operations, not a shared misleading label.
- **Playback toolbar below the display:** Play/Pause, Reset, a compact accessible mute/unmute button plus inline volume slider (retain existing volume range/behavior), display preset selector and fullscreen. Group these like snes-rust. Optional display sizing (Fit/native scale) is fine only if useful and coherent; prioritize the fit-to-viewport layout rather than adding another setting by default. Display a short live status without causing layout shifts; show errors/recovery only when relevant.
- **Secondary settings:** compact Settings disclosure/popover for boot source, Restore FreeDOS HDD, optional RGB phosphor mask and other infrequent settings. Keep the active/next boot source clear and distinguish it from the selected disk insertion target. Place Ap mouse enable/disable in an easily discoverable input/settings location (visible when relevant); retain the existing semantics.
- **Keyboard:** collapsed by default on a desktop, one obvious button/disclosure to reveal the existing PC-98 virtual keyboard. Preserve the complete key mapping, modifier combinations, physical keyboard and mouse support. On touch devices ensure the keyboard is readily available, including an appropriate keyboard toggle and practical access while fullscreen; do not blindly transplant an SNES gamepad.

## Media interactions and behavior

Use snes-rust's compact cartridge picker as a reference for a PC-98 **media picker**, using an accessible native popover/dialog or equivalent.

- Each drive has a clearly scoped Insert/Change action and local file selection; the picker closes on Escape/outside click, preserves the current mounted media on dismissal/cancel, returns focus sensibly, and never pauses/resets the guest solely because a picker was opened or canceled.
- Retain current drag-and-drop auto routing (HDI/NHD -> HDD, supported floppy images -> FDD1), explicit destination overrides for FDD1/FDD2/HDD and appropriate errors for incompatible file types/machines. Provide a clear auto-insert path if needed without bringing back a large ambiguous shared control row.
- Preserve existing PC-9821Ap default auto-boot with bundled writable FreeDOS HDD and VM/Ap profile behavior. Floppy insertion is not a boot command. Boot-source selection changes the next reset, not the running guest. Do not silently reboot on unrelated settings changes. HDD replacement and demo launch retain their existing intentional reboot semantics.
- Keep Star Trail and Hello world + BEEP accessible from a compact demo/media picker or clearly labeled secondary demo action; communicate that launching a demo boots it instead of mounting a normal data floppy.
- Retain all current supported disk formats, chunked HDI/NHD import/export and per-slot names, progress/errors, dirty-HDD discard confirmation and export-before-replace recovery path. Canceling a destructive confirmation must preserve the current disk and guest. Restore FreeDOS remains available but cannot bypass existing confirmation. Keep all local disk bytes in the browser; no uploads or new persistence for guest data.
- Disable only appropriate controls during initialization or transactions, prevent overlapping/destructive operations, and avoid incorrect stale UI after profile/reset/boot changes. Retain current visibility/audio permission behavior unless a separately justified UX change is explicitly documented and tested.

## Responsive and accessibility requirements

- **Desktop:** two-column layout with stable screen/slot geometry. Compact toolbar; right panel may use an adaptive width. Long filenames, errors, status changes or opening Help must not resize the guest screen unexpectedly.
- **Phone/tablet portrait:** screen first, playback toolbar immediately below, then media/machine controls and on-demand keyboard/settings. Fit the viewport width, no horizontal page overflow, no obscured canvas, readable controls. Avoid forcing all PC-98 keys permanently onto a small screen.
- **Short landscape/touch:** prioritize screen area; use compact side or below-screen controls as space permits. Preserve visible fullscreen exit and usable touch input, safe-area insets, and aspect ratio. Allow secondary settings/keyboard to expand or scroll intentionally rather than clipping controls.
- Use CSS Grid/Flexbox, sensible breakpoints and viewport-relative sizing, keeping the layout stable across resize/orientation changes. Use semantic HTML, visible focus, keyboard-operable dialogs, labeled controls, appropriate ARIA pressed/expanded/state/live attributes, readable contrast and comfortable touch targets (aim for 44×44 CSS px for primary touch actions). Preserve canvas focus and guest input, avoid stuck keys on blur/overlay transitions, and do not send host UI keystrokes into the guest.
- Keep long technical explanations out of the normal player view, but show actionable errors, destructive warnings and license/help links where needed.

## Architecture / scope

This is a **frontend UI/UX/layout redesign**, principally `web/index.html`, `web/style.css`, `web/app.js`, and relevant frontend tests/docs. Reuse existing presenter, Worker message protocols and disk/guest state as the authority; keep raw canvas and CRT overlay behavior, frame credit/recycling, JIT defaults, CPU timing, AudioWorklet, OPNA stereo, volume controls, and performance optimizations intact.

Preserve **Sharp CRT as the default**, saved display preferences, optional RGB mask, raw/unfiltered screenshots, existing WebGL/software fallback and adaptive presentation behavior. Switching display modes/fullscreen must not restart the guest. Do not add CPU-side filters, heavy UI frameworks, remote assets, dependencies or unnecessary polling. Preserve GitHub Pages at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, site security, first-party assets and license boundaries.

Prefer a cohesive small UI-state model and reuse existing actions rather than duplicating the emulator or creating parallel media lifecycles. Existing element IDs/test hooks may be retained where sensible; where changed, migrate browser tests to the real new user flow rather than bypassing it.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deliver the screen-first snes-rust-inspired design: compact header, screen + right-side machine/media slots on desktop, grouped playback controls below, secondary settings/Help, no large introductory/technical prose in the main player.
- [ ] Verify actual normal release-Wasm browser operation from initial FreeDOS boot, both demo launch paths, VM/Ap selection, drag/drop and explicit FDD1/FDD2/HDD routing, file chooser cancel, insert/eject/export, dirty HDD replacement/restore cancel/confirm, separate boot selection and Reset. Check real media/guest state, not only mocked UI events.
- [ ] Verify pause/resume, audio activation/mute/volume (including stereo), all CRT presets/default/persistence/fallback, fullscreen/exit, physical/virtual keyboard, mouse and focus, including interaction with open popovers and canceled selections.
- [ ] Use representative desktop and responsive sizes (at least 1280×720, 1440×900, phone portrait ~390×844 and phone landscape ~844×390, plus a narrow ~320px viewport), validate geometry/no horizontal overflow, control visibility, stable screen size with long names/status and safe touch interaction. Capture before/after screenshots with original or rights-cleared guest fixtures only; record design decisions and evidence. No proprietary game images or media in Git or CI artifacts.
- [ ] Check keyboard-only navigation, focus return, accessible names, meaningful warnings and error recovery. Touch controls remain usable in normal and fullscreen modes.
- [ ] Preserve existing native/core, release-Wasm, browser, serial audio, CRT/presenter, media safety and publication checks at both serving roots. Re-run normal browser performance/audio smoke tests to show no new material throughput or audio continuity regression; do not weaken existing assertions, timeouts, or thresholds to make the redesign pass.
- [ ] Update README/help and relevant validation notes to describe the actual new layout/workflows, including insertion vs boot, local media safety, and CRT default. Run repository-standard review/build/test procedures. Record any remaining limitations.

## Non-goals

No redesign of the underlying CPU/emulated hardware, new shader algorithms, new file formats, permanent disk persistence, game library/cloud service, or unrelated feature work. No need to change the author's snes-rust repository. The objective is a cleaner, intuitive **PC-98 player**, not a generic emulator configuration dashboard.

## Required post-merge verification
